summary: The skills disagree about who may set a gate to Done, and gate review depends on a SOP that is not in the plugin, so a pass can rest on a partial checklist. Precheck writes pasted output into the project before screening it, requires Cloud SQL provider files for every database, and treats several conditions as upgrade blockers that the cited source rows do not support.

findings.claim: Parsing starts by writing the pasted precheck into upgrade/results/ unchanged, and only the later Don't section says to stop when that paste contains row data or query text. Following the numbered steps stores regulated data or secrets in the project, which the always-on guardrail forbids.
findings.evidence: Skill: "Save the input to `upgrade/results/` unchanged, with one file per database or output." Later: "Don't copy row data or query text into the report. If the paste contains any, stop and ask for a clean rerun." Guardrail in plugins/pg-major-upgrade/rules/guardrails.mdc: "Don't put row data, query text, patient or customer records, or secrets into prompts, files, the tracker or Slack. If pasted output contains row data, stop and ask for a version without it." The skill never says to delete a file already saved.
findings.suggested_fix: Screen the paste before any write. If it contains row data, query text, or secrets, do not put it under upgrade/; ask for a clean rerun and delete any file already written.

findings.claim: Gate pass and fail decisions depend entirely on ../../reference/sop.md, which is not in the plugin, and the skill does not say to stop when that file is missing. The only criteria written in the skill are labeled as checks that often fail, so an agent can pass a gate without the SOP's exit conditions.
findings.evidence: Skill: "The gates and what each needs are in `../../reference/sop.md`, in each block's exit gates table." plugins/pg-major-upgrade/reference/ contains only tracker-schema.md. The same skill says "Checks that often fail" and lists G0.2, G0.5, G1.1, G2.1, and G2.6, then still requires a verdict of "pass", "fail", or "needs decision". No step says a missing SOP fails the review.
findings.suggested_fix: Ship the SOP next to the skill, and if it cannot be opened, write the report as fail and do not issue pass. Do not treat the short failure list as the full exit criteria.

findings.claim: The precheck, tracker, and gate-review skills give contradictory orders about setting a gate to Done, so a gate can be closed with no owner or can never be closed by following all three. The needs-decision verdict is also not mapped to a tracker status, and the report's can-exit line is not tied to the sign-off step 3 requires.
findings.evidence: Precheck skill: "Set G0.2 to `Done` only if every part-1 check passed" and "Never set G0.3, G0.4 or G0.5 to `Done` from this skill." Gate review: "Never set a gate to `Done` yourself. The named owner or approver does that, and the tracker skill records who." It maps pass to Needs approval and fail to Blocked, and does not mention needs decision. Tracker skill: "Gates close through `pg-upgrade-gate-review`" and "Don't mark anything `Done` without evidence, or close gates." Gate review also says a block exits only when every gate "is `pass` and has its sign-off", while the report only needs a "can exit" or "can't exit" line.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one path: agents never set a gate to Done; the tracker skill may set Done only after a named approver and an evidence link. Map needs decision to Needs approval, and allow "can exit" only after that sign-off is recorded.

findings.claim: The catch-up description says the skill marks gates with evidence, but the steps say gates stay open until gate review. A decision can also be set to Done when the handoff names a person, with no Evidence field, which the tracker checker rejects for every Done row.
findings.evidence: Description: "Maps the handoff's facts, decisions, open questions and prior results into project.json and the tracker, and marks gates with evidence." Step 5: "Gates stay open until `pg-upgrade-gate-review` runs." Step 3: "Its status is `Done` only if the handoff names the decider." tracker-lib.mjs: "Done without Evidence; set it to Needs approval until evidence is linked". Step 3 also says a statement is recorded "not as evidence."
findings.suggested_fix: Change the description so it does not say the skill marks gates. Set a decision to Done only when the handoff identifies the decider and an evidence link, and otherwise use Needs approval.

findings.claim: The guide says has_generated_columns = t fails the Cloud SQL upgrade and cites S-01, but the S-01 row does not mention generated columns. The flag is also written only on the unlogged-table row, so a reader can miss it on ordinary tables or open a false G0.4 blocker.
findings.evidence: Guide: "`has_generated_columns = t` fails the Cloud SQL upgrade [S-01]. Both are blockers (G0.4)." S-01 supports text lists MVU limits, extension floors, blocking flags, large objects, database count, and relation count, and its quotes include "vacuum_defer_cleanup_age" and "more than 10 million large objects, then the upgrade fails", but not generated columns. The live Cloud SQL page could not be fetched in this review.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the generated-column blocker unless a quote is added to S-01. If it is real, give it its own check for every table, not only section 5b.

findings.claim: Section 6a says any composite row blocks pg_upgrade and cites S-22. The S-22 row supports aclitem and reg* types, not composite types, so a normal composite column can be filed as a hard upgrade blocker.
findings.evidence: Guide: "6a. reg*, aclitem, composite | Empty | Any row blocks pg_upgrade [S-22]". S-22 supports: "Checks pg_upgrade 18 runs: NOT NULL inheritance, aclitem and reg* types, prepared transactions, datallowconn, output_plugin_libraries." Quotes include "incompatible \"aclitem\" data type" and "regcollation", not composite. The live check.c page could not be fetched in this review.
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the pg_upgrade blocker to the types S-22 actually names. If the kit emits a separate composite result, say what that result means and do not call every row a blocker.

findings.claim: The only fix given for a NOT NULL inheritance hit is to add SET NOT NULL. The cited failure is an inconsistency, and the guide does not say what to do when nulls are present or when the extra constraint is on the child, so the reader can run the wrong ALTER.
findings.evidence: Guide: "Blocks pg_upgrade 18 [S-22]. Add `SET NOT NULL` after checking for nulls." S-22 quote: "Your installation contains inconsistent NOT NULL constraints". The quote does not say the constraint is always missing on the child. The live check.c page could not be fetched in this review.
findings.suggested_fix: Tell the reader to compare parent and child, and to stop for a DBA when the column contains nulls or the child is the stricter side, instead of prescribing only SET NOT NULL.

findings.claim: Every precheck run is invalid unless Cloud SQL precheck JSON, operations describe, and instances describe are present. Bootstrap accepts any provider, so an RDS, Azure, or self-hosted upgrade can never pass the G0.2 check this skill uses.
findings.evidence: Reading guide part 1, required for every run: "Provider outputs present | Precheck JSON, `operations describe` JSON, `instances describe` YAML | Can't say whether the provider will start the upgrade." Precheck skill: "Set G0.2 to `Done` only if every part-1 check passed". The same skill's request section says "On Cloud SQL that's `gcloud sql instances pre-check-major-version-upgrade`" and does not say what a non-Cloud SQL provider must supply. Bootstrap's provider field is free text.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the Cloud SQL files required only when the provider is Cloud SQL. For any other provider, record the provider check as not applicable or ask for that provider's documented precheck, and do not fail G0.2 for missing gcloud output.

findings.claim: Blockers and prework are filed to G0.3 or G0.4, but neither skill says which findings belong to which gate. A blocker attached to the wrong gate makes the other gate look clear.
findings.evidence: Precheck skill: "Set `Gates` to G0.3 or G0.4". Reading guide: blockers are "the gate it feeds (G0.3 or G0.4)" and, for section 5b only, "Both are blockers (G0.4)." No skill or tracker schema defines G0.3 versus G0.4. Gate review's G1.1 note mentions provider precheck and sections 3 and 5b without naming those gates.
findings.suggested_fix: State the rule in the precheck skill, for example provider errors to one gate and catalog blockers to the other, and point at the SOP section that defines each gate's Done when.

findings.claim: During cutover the scribe records a step as done when a person says it is done, and alarms only if the step runs long. The draft requires an expected output for every step, but the scribe never compares the output to it, so a failed command can be written down as complete.
findings.evidence: Section C: "When a person reports a step done, record the time and the output summary. Flag any step running past its rehearsed time plus 25%, and remind the go or no-go owner of the latest rollback decision time." Section A requires "its command for a person to run, its expected output". The scribe steps do not say an error, or output that does not match, means the step is not done and the checkpoint is no-go. There is also no instruction to keep row data out of the output summary.
findings.suggested_fix: Before recording a step done, compare the reported output to the expected output. On a mismatch or error, leave the step open and ask the go or no-go owner for an explicit no-go. Store a redacted summary, not raw output.

findings.claim: Catch-up tells the agent to skip bootstrap's repo search until after step 7, but step 8 is the stop and forbids new work until the program owner confirms. The consumer search therefore has no step in which it is allowed to run.
findings.evidence: Step 1: "Skip its repo search until after step 7 below." Step 7 is validate and render. Step 8: "Ask the program owner to confirm the summary before you start any new work." Bootstrap step 4, the search that was skipped, is what adds Consumer rows for G0.1. Nothing after the confirmation says to resume that search.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the repo search its own step after the owner confirms the handoff summary, or run it before the stop and include the hits in the summary that the owner confirms.

findings.claim: The skills order the agent to read and run plugin files that are not in this package, and they do not say what to do when a path is missing. An agent cannot draft the kit request, seed the tracker, check it, or render the dashboard by following the steps.
findings.evidence: Precheck: "The kit is `../../assets/precheck.sql`" and "cite `../../reference/sources.md`". Those paths are absent. plugins/pg-major-upgrade/reference/ has only tracker-schema.md. The only script present is scripts/tracker-lib.mjs; tracker-check.mjs, render-dashboard.mjs, run-review-round.sh, review-with-cursor.sh, and review-with-codex.sh are not. Bootstrap copies `../../assets/tracker.csv`, which is absent. Model review cites `../../agents/findings.schema.json`, which is absent (independent-reviewer.md is present). sources.json actually lives at review/reference/sources.json, while the evidence rule and the skills say sources.md and sop-auditor says reference/sources.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the kit, seed tracker, SOP, source list, checker, dashboard renderer, and review scripts at the paths the skills name, or stop with a named missing file instead of continuing. Use one filename for the source register.

findings.claim: The review command says every path is relative to the skill, but the script path and the upgrade/ paths are not relative to the same directory. The same split is in every skill that runs node ../../scripts/... upgrade/tracker.csv, so the checker and the review round fail from either the skill directory or the workspace root.
findings.evidence: Model review: "Paths are relative to this skill" after `../../scripts/run-review-round.sh gate upgrade/reviews/<artifact>-<YYYY-MM-DD> upgrade/decision-record.md`. From the skill directory, ../../scripts is plugins/pg-major-upgrade/scripts, while upgrade/ is at the workspace root, four levels up. Tracker skill: "Run `node ../../scripts/tracker-check.mjs upgrade/tracker.csv`" with no working directory stated. Workspace layout says plugin files are relative to the skill and project files live in upgrade/ at the workspace root.
findings.suggested_fix: State the working directory, or pass workspace-root paths for upgrade files and plugin-root paths for scripts. If the canvases directory does not exist, leave the dashboard under upgrade/ and say so.

findings.claim: Bootstrap and the tracker skill persist and read trackerBackend, but the tracker schema tells the agent to set tracker_backend. A project can point at Sheets or Notion under one key while the skill updates the CSV under the other.
findings.evidence: Bootstrap writes `trackerBackend` (default `project`). Tracker skill: "The tracker is `upgrade/tracker.csv` unless `upgrade/project.json` sets `trackerBackend`." Tracker schema: "set `tracker_backend` in the bootstrap prompt". The bootstrap prompt itself only says "Tracker: {{project | sheets | notion | linear | jira}}" and does not name the JSON key.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one field name in the schema, the bootstrap skill, and project.json, and have the tracker skill read only that field before choosing CSV or an MCP backend.

findings.claim: When a reviewer fails, the skill says to report the error file and continue. It never says a round with no successful reviewer must block sign-off, so an empty reconciliation leaves the gate with no confirmed blockers.
findings.evidence: "A reviewer that fails leaves a `.err` file. Report it, and continue with the others." Step 5: "The gate can't pass while a confirmed blocker is open." There is no minimum number of successful reviews and no instruction for the case where every reviewer fails or the script is missing. The description says to use the skill "before signing off a gate".
findings.suggested_fix: If fewer than the required reviewers return a schema-valid report, write the round as failed and do not treat the gate as clear. Do not reconcile an empty set into zero blockers.

findings.claim: The guide says a row with relkind = p is an unlogged partitioned table that PostgreSQL 18 refuses. relkind p means partitioned, logged or unlogged; the S-17 quote does not mention relkind. Applied outside section 5b, ordinary partitioned tables become blockers.
findings.evidence: Guide: "A row with `relkind = p` is an unlogged partitioned table, which 18 refuses [S-17]." S-17 quote: "Disallow unlogged partitioned tables". The live pg_class page (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/catalog-pg-class.html) could not be fetched in this review. Section 5b is titled Unlogged, but section 2c is a separate partitioned-table section and is not tied to this sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that within the unlogged result, relpersistence unlogged plus relkind p is the PostgreSQL 18 refusal, and that relkind p alone does not block.

findings.claim: The guide says any large object blocks logical paths, and that DMS drops updates and deletes on keyless tables even with full or index replica identity. S-13's stored quotes support a large-object limitation and keyless update/delete loss, not those stronger wordings.
findings.evidence: Guide: "Any large objects at all block logical paths [S-13]." Section 5a: "tables without a primary key lose UPDATEs and DELETEs even with `full` or `index` identity [S-13]". S-13 quotes: "UPDATE and DELETE statements aren't migrated for tables without primary keys" and "Large Object data type". Neither quote mentions replica identity or says any large object blocks the path. The live DMS page could not be fetched in this review.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the S-13 wording: large objects are a logical-migration limitation, and keyless tables lose updates and deletes on DMS. Keep the note to check replica identity only for non-DMS tools, without the unsupported "even with" clause.

findings.claim: Catch-up points at a handoff template that is not in the repo. The skill says an unmatched handoff still works, but the agent has no shape to compare against when it lists what is missing.
findings.evidence: "The expected shape of a handoff is in the template's `docs/catch-up-handoff-template.md`." review/docs/ contains automations.md and bootstrap-prompt.md only. bootstrap-prompt.md also links to catch-up-handoff-template.md, and that file is absent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add docs/catch-up-handoff-template.md, or replace the reference with the field list the skill already uses so a missing template is not an input.

findings.claim: The tracker skill posts the daily summary to Slack when the program owner has turned that on, but the /pg-status command tells the agent not to post unless the person who invoked it asks. An agent that loads both can send the summary on a status check the user wanted only in chat.
findings.evidence: Tracker skill: "Post it to the project's Slack channel only if the program owner has turned that on. Otherwise put it in chat." Command plugins/pg-major-upgrade/commands/pg-status.md: "Show the summary in chat. Don't post it to Slack unless I ask." Automations.md also posts the weekday summary to the channel.
findings.suggested_fix: State one rule: a scheduled job may post after the program owner opts in, and an interactive /pg-status run posts only when that message asks for Slack.
